title: Take-Two CEO on GTA 6 and AI: Making Hits Still Requires Humans
description: During Take-Two's Q2 2027 earnings call, CEO Strauss Zelnick addressed investor concerns about AI and piracy, emphasizing that hit games require human creativity.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Take-Two Earnings Call Addresses AI and the Future

During Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, CEO Strauss Zelnick fielded questions from investors following the presentation of the company's financial results. As anticipation continues to build around upcoming titles like *GTA 6*, financial stakeholders are increasingly interested in how major publishing houses plan to navigate the rapid evolution of technology and security in the modern gaming landscape.

## Investor Concerns Over AI-Powered Compilation and Piracy

Among the topics raised during the Q&A session, one caller specifically addressed the growing proliferation of AI. The concern centered around AI-powered compilations and decompilations, a technological trend that has been raising significant piracy concerns for publishers over the past few weeks. As automated code analysis advances, the industry faces new questions regarding digital rights management and software protection.

## Human Creativity at the Core of Game Development

Responding to the inquiry, Strauss Zelnick reaffirmed his confidence in developer creativity. He emphasized that the complex process of making hit games "remains the purview of human beings." This statement underscores Take-Two's ongoing reliance on human talent and artistic vision to drive top-tier entertainment properties forward, signaling that while technology evolves, the core of blockbuster game creation still depends heavily on human ingenuity.

## Editor's Take

As the games industry grapples with the disruptive potential of artificial intelligence, leadership's stance on human creativity is vital. Zelnick's comments offer reassurance that major players like Rockstar Games and Take-Two still value artisan-level direction over automated shortcuts when crafting industry-defining hits.
